title: Proving Termination Check
description: Name progress measures and spot loops that may not halt.

questions.prompt: Binary search terminates because each branch:

options.text: Strictly shrinks the integer window `hi - lo + 1`

questions.explanation: Progress measure: window size `hi - lo + 1`. Setting `lo = mid + 1` or `hi = mid - 1` strictly shrinks a non-negative integer window.

questions.prompt: `while (i < arr.length) { if (rare) continue; i++; }` is dangerous because:

options.text: Some paths may never move `i` — no guaranteed progress

questions.explanation: Bad pattern — no guaranteed shrink. All branches must make progress, including `continue` paths.

options.text: What decreases, that it is bounded, and that all branches progress

questions.explanation: Checklist: what quantity decreases (or advances), is it bounded, and do all branches make progress?

questions.prompt: Why prefer integer progress measures over `x /= 2` floats near zero?
questions.explanation: Floating-point “shrink” (`x /= 2`) can misbehave near zero; prefer integer measures when possible.
